the_ruling_verbatim: every feedback was probably a probe reporting in.

we identified 2 kinds of consumers for feedback. Active ones and passive ones. active ones can get feedback, and within their own structure, however that may work, AI or not, the reciever can assess the feedback and act on it. Sending an entire ticket back to design is that kind of feedback, in that design then comes before you and i, who can act on it.

but an inspector is not that kind of animal. it can recieve feedback to a mailbox/data recorder (a tool we specified but i haven't checked to see if it was ticketed or built) that would just record all the feedback until an LLM inspection pass later to evaluate the feedback and see if we needed to alter the questions the inspector is asking.
so for the specific case you described, i'd say it would need an extra probe for each thing it wanted to report back to.
now_the_spec_says: Feedback IS probes. Multiple targets = multiple probes, not a split edge. Two consumer kinds: ACTIVE (can act) and PASSIVE (mailbox/data recorder, LLM reviews later). One probe per reporting target.
what_this_does_to_the_prior_ruling: RESOLVES the question posed by ticket a-segments-outbound-edge-carries-one-address. The three options CC offered (keep one address, key by finding subject, key by caller) are all superseded: the edge stays one address because the probe is the mechanism, and multiple probes (not a split edge) handle multiple targets. Also connects to scheduled-llm-gate-inspection, which is the consumption side of the passive-consumer case — that ticket's 'gate collects feedback in a shape Hex can read' is the data recorder's write path.
